## 1.1 Document Purpose
The purpose of this document is to specify the software requirements for Pontis, a mobile language learning application design, as a crash course for travelers. It describes what the system does, the interface it depends on, and the reader should have a clear understanding of the applications' scope from both the users and the developer's perspective. 
## 1.2 Product Scope
Pontis prepares the travelers for a trip to a country they have never visited by teaching the basic phrases needed to introduce themselves, navigate, order food, buy things, and ask how things work, what to expect in order to respond. For each supported language, content is organized into three modules (introduction, Navigation, and Business). Each Module contains Lessons, each Lesson contains classes, and each module ends with a Test.   

- **Onboarding and Authentication**: Users create an account with an email and password or single sign-on, select a language, manage account settings, log out, and permanently delete their account.

- **Flashcards:** Users study two-sided vocabulary and grammar cards and rate their recall, which schedules future reviews using spaced repetition.

- **Fill-in-blank:** Users complete sentences by selecting words from a word bank and receive immediate feedback.

- **Pronunciation**: Users speak target phrases and receive a pass or fail result based on on-device speech recognition

- **Module Tests**: Users complete a multiple-choice Test at the end of each Module, using image, real-world scenario, and audio listening questions

- **Progression and analytics:** users view their completion and test results by language, module, competency score. 

**The following are outside of scope for this product:**

- **Gamification features such as streak, points and badges**

## 1.3 Intended Audience
This document is intended for language learners seeking a structured progression with clear goals, as well as developers who will design and implement the system, and testers who will verify that it meets all functional requirements.

## 1.4 Definition, Acronyms, and Abbreviations. 
*Definitions of key terms, acronyms, and internal naming conventions are used across PONTIS to ensure shared understanding.*

| **Term** | **Definition** |
| --- | --- |
| Pontis | The name of the mobile language-learning application |
| User | A person with a registered account who uses the application  |
| Lesson | A group of Classes within a Module that builds toward a set of needed phrases |
| Class | A single practice activity within a Lesson, of one exercise type: flashcards, fill-in-the-blank, or pronunciation. Not to be confused with a programming class |
| Test | A multiple-choice assessment at the end of each Module |
| Component | A major system feature: Onboarding and Authentication, Flashcards, Fill-in-the-Blank, Pronunciation, Module Tests, or Progression and Analytics |
| FSRS | Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler, the algorithm that schedules flashcard reviews |
| SSO | Single sign-on |
| Vosk | Offline speech recognition toolkit used for on-device pronunciation checking |

The documents and online resources cited in this specification are listed in Section 6 (References). The structure of this document follows IEEE Std 830-1998, and requirement wording follows the guidance of K. E. Wiegers, "Writing Quality Requirements." Technical references for the chosen platform (Flutter and Supabase) and for the diagramming tool (Mermaid) are also listed in Section 6.
## 1.6 Overview and Document Conventions
The remainder of this document is organized as follows. Section 2 gives an overall description of the product, its users, and its constraints. Section 3 contains the specific requirements: external interfaces, functional requirements organized by component, performance requirements, logical database requirements, and design constraints. Section 4 defines the software system attributes (non-functional requirements). Section 5 presents the class diagrams that model the system, and Section 6 lists the references.

Conventions: the word "shall" marks a mandatory requirement. The application is referred to as Pontis or "the system." Terms defined in Section 1.4 (such as Module, Lesson, Class, and Test) are capitalized when used in their defined sense. Class diagrams use UML class notation.

## 2.1 Product Perspective
The language learning application is a standalone educational mobile application designed to help users learn and practice foreign languages through short, interactive lessons. The application will provide functionality similar to existing language-learning platforms such as Duolingo, including structured lessons, vocabulary and grammar exercises, progress tracking. 

The system will consist of a client-side user interface and a backend service responsible for user accounts, lesson content, progress data, and application state. User data will be stored in a persistent database so that progress can be synchronized across supported devices. The application may also interact with external services for authentication, notifications, analytics, or other supporting functionality.

The application will be designed so that additional languages, lessons, exercises, and features can be added without requiring major changes to the existing system.
## 2.2 Product Functions
The application shall provide the following primary functions: 

- **User Account Management** 

  - Allow users to create, log in to, and log out of accounts. 

  - Allow users to manage basic account and profile information. 

  - Store and synchronize user learning progress. 

- **Language Selection** 

  - Allow users to select a language they wish to learn. 

  - Allow users to learn multiple languages using the same account. 

- **Lessons and Exercises** 

  - Provide lessons organized into modules that contains classes and tests for each language. 

  - Present exercises involving vocabulary, grammar, reading, writing, listening, and translation. 

  - Users will be tested on their language competency at the end of each module.

  - Allow users to retry lessons or exercises upon completion of module.

- **Progress Tracking** 

  - Track completed modules, lessons, classes, and competency scores.

  - Display the user's overall learning progress. 

- **Review and Practice** 

  - Provide review exercises for previously learned material. 

  - Identify areas in which a user has made mistakes and provide additional practice. 

  - Provide additional cultural and grammatical context for certain linguistic phrases and when is most appropriate to use them.

- **Learner Motivation** 

  - Record completed lesson modules and display completion status to encourage users to continue their progress (gamification features such as streaks, points, and badges are out of scope; see Section 1.2).

  - Encourage users to practice their newly acquired language competency skills by practicing with native speakers.

- **Notifications (future release; see Section 2.7)** 

  - Provide optional reminders encouraging users to continue their learning activities. 

  - Notify users of relevant progress or achievement events. 

  - Notify users of nearby locations to practice their language skills.  

- **Settings** 

  - Allow users to configure application preferences. 

  - Allow users to manage notification preferences. 

  - Provide options for managing account-related settings.

  - Allow users to toggle microphone access on hardware devices.
## 2.3 User Characteristics
The primary users of the application will be individuals who want or have an immediate need to learn or practice a foreign language (i.e. tourists in a non-English speaking country). Users may have widely varying levels of language proficiency and computer literacy.

 

The system is intended to accommodate:

 

- Beginning learners with little or no previous knowledge of the selected language.

- Casual learners who want to practice general or most used phrases.

- Regular learners who use the application as part of a structured language-learning routine.

- Learners who wish to navigate a non-English speaking country or participate in local and cultural norms.

- Learners already familiar with the language who wish to gain a better understanding of it.

 

Users are expected to have basic familiarity with smartphones, tablets, or computers and common interface elements such as buttons, menus, text fields, and navigation controls. No specialized technical knowledge should be required.

 

The application may also be used by instructors or administrators if such functionality is included in later versions. Administrative users would have additional permissions for managing language-learning content and monitoring system operation.
## 2.4 Operating Environment & User Interfaces
The application shall operate on commonly used consumer computing platforms. 	The target environment will include:

- Modern **Android and iOS mobile devices**. 

- Modern **Android and iOS tablets**, using the same responsive layout as phones.

- Internet connectivity for account synchronization, downloading lesson content, and storing progress. 

The application interface shall provide a simple, consistent, and accessible user 	experience.

The primary user interfaces shall include:

1. **Login/Registration Interface** 

   1. Account creation and authentication. 

   2. Password and account recovery functionality. 

2. **Home/Dashboard Interface** 

   3. Current learning progress. 

   4. Available languages to learn and lesson modules for each language. 

   5. Navigation to other application functions. 

3. **Module Interface** 

   6. Presentation of lesson content, classes, and competency tests. 

   7. Answer submission controls. 

   8. Immediate feedback. 

   9. Progress through the current module. 

4. **Progress Interface** 

   10. Completed lesson modules.

   11. Learning statistics and competency scores.

5. **Profile and Settings Interface** 

   12. Account information. 

   13. Language preferences. 

   14. Notification and application settings. 

   15. Microphone accessibility settings.

The user interface should support different screen sizes and should be designed to 	remain usable on both phone and tablet displays.
## 2.5 Design and Implementation Constraints
The following constraints shall apply to the design and implementation of the 		system:

- The application shall require an internet connection for functions that depend on the backend server, such as account synchronization and retrieval of new content. 

- User authentication and personal data shall be handled securely. 

- Passwords shall not be stored as plaintext. 

- Communication between the client application and backend services shall use secure communication protocols such as HTTPS. 

- The system shall use a persistent database for storing user accounts, learning progress, lesson information, and other required data. 

- The application shall be designed using a modular architecture to allow future addition of languages and learning features. 

- The interface shall be designed to accommodate different screen sizes and supported platforms. 

- The system shall provide reasonable response times for common user actions under normal network conditions. 

- The application shall comply with applicable privacy and data-protection requirements. 

- The implementation shall use technologies and frameworks compatible with the project's development environment and deployment requirements.

 

## 2.6 Assumptions and Dependencies
The following assumptions and dependencies are made regarding the system:

**Assumptions**

- Users have access to a supported device and a reasonably reliable internet connection. 

- Users will provide accurate account information when creating an account. 

- Users have basic familiarity with operating a smartphone, tablet, or computer. 

- Lesson content will be prepared and reviewed before being made available to users. 

- The application will primarily be used for independent, self-directed learning. 

- Users will have sufficient audio capability, such as speakers or headphones, when completing listening exercises. 

**Dependencies**

- The application depends on a backend server or cloud service for account management and synchronization of user data. 

- The application depends on a database service for persistent storage. 

- Mobile versions depend on the relevant mobile operating systems and their supported APIs. 

- If push notifications are supported, the application depends on the notification services provided by the target operating systems. 

- Audio-based exercises depend on the availability of appropriate audio files or speech-processing services. 

- The application may depend on third-party authentication, analytics, cloud storage, or other external services.

## 2.7 Apportioning of Requirements
Requirements that are not part of the initial release are deferred to later versions of Pontis. The deferred items are:

- Push notifications and reminders, including progress or achievement alerts and prompts for nearby places to practice (Section 2.2, Notifications).

- Instructor and administrator roles for managing content and monitoring the system (Section 2.3).

- Reading, writing, and free-form translation exercises (Section 2.2). The initial release provides flashcards, fill-in-the-blank exercises, pronunciation practice, and Module Tests with image, scenario, and audio listening questions.

- Native desktop or laptop client applications (Section 2.4). The initial release targets Android and iOS phones and tablets.

- Gamification features such as streaks, points, and badges, which remain out of scope (Section 1.2).

All requirements in Section 3 and Section 4 apply to the initial release.

## 3. Specific Requirements
## 3.1 External Interface Requirements
### 3.1.1 User Interface
- **Onboarding & Setup Screens**

  - The system shall provide user login, sign-up, and onboarding screens

  - The system shall provide a dedicated language selection screen allowing user to choose their active target language

- **Curriculum & Navigation Interfaces**

  - The system shall display a module overview screen detailing user completion across three primary modules: Introduction, Navigation, and Business.

  - The system shall provide hierarchical navigation screens displaying lessons, and the individual classes contained within each lesson.

- **Interactive Exercise Interfaces**

  - The system shall provide a touch-responsive flashcard interface supporting tap-to-flip and swipe-to-navigate touch gestures.

  - The system shall present a tap-to-select word-tile interface for fill-in-the-blank sentence completion exercises.

  - The system shall provide a microphone recording interface displaying real-time visual recording indicators during audio pronunciation practice.

- **Assessment & Test Screens**

  - The system shall render test screens supporting image-based prompts, scenario text for real-world interaction questions, and embedded audio playback controls for listening comprehension questions.

  - The system shall display multiple-choice selection buttons on test screens and automatically transition to a results screen displaying a competency score.

- **Progress & Analytics Dashboard**

  - The system shall display a central progress dashboard summarizing course completion percentage, competency scores.

- **System Alerts & Feedback Displays**

  - The system shall render clear on-screen notifications when network connectivity is lost or when necessary; device permissions (Microphone access) are denied.

### 3.1.2 Hardware Interface
- **Audio Input Interface (Microphone)**

  - The system shall interface with the device microphone to capture user voice input during pronunciation practice and speech exercises.

- **Audio Output Interface (Speaker / Headphones)**

  - The system shall interface with the device speaker and headphone output to play native speaker audio samples, sentence pronunciations and audio prompts for test questions.

- **Touchscreen Display Interface**

  - The system shall interface with the device touchscreen to register user touch interactions (taps, flips, and swipes) and display UI screens, text prompts, and test images.

### 3.1.3 Software Interface
- **Cloud Backend & Authentication API (Supabase)**

  - The system shall interface with hosted Supabase REST APIs to perform user authentication, deliver lesson and test curriculum content, and persist user progress data.

- **Speech Recognition & Pronunciation Processing Engines**

  - The system shall interface with the Vosk engine for on-device speech recognition with Architecture that could implement openAI whisper.

  - The system shall interface with the Azure Speech Pronunciation Assessment service to process user voice recordings and generate phoneme-level pronunciation accuracy scores.

- **Database Management System (PostgreSQL)**

  - The system shall interface with a hosted PostgresSQL relational database (via SupaBase) to manage persistent user profiles, content structure, class records, and progress logs. 

- **Cloud Asset Storage Service (Supabase Storage)**

  - The system shall interface with Supabase Storage to stream and cache media assets—including image files and Mozilla Common Voice / Wikimedia audio clips—for lesson exercises and tests.
## 
### 3.1.4 Communications Interfaces
- **Secure Network Transmission**

  - The system shall conduct all communications between the mobile application and backend services (Supabase REST API, Authentication, and Storage) over HTTPS encrypted with TLS 1.3 protocol.

- **Backend Proxy & API Key Protection**

  - The system shall route pronunciation assessment requests to Azure Speech Services via a backend Supabase Edge Function over HTTPS, ensuring third-party API service keys are never embedded or exposed within the mobile client application.

- **Background Asset Synchronization**

  - The system shall download lesson and test media assets (images and audio) over HTTPS from Supabase Storage, supporting background downloads for full offline availability.

- **Connection Resilience & Download Resumption**

  - The system shall detect network interruptions during media asset downloads and automatically resume fetching from the point of failure upon reconnection without re-downloading previously transferred data.

- **Bandwidth Optimization & Offline Processing**

  - **The system shall optimize text curriculum data (Lessons, classes, test) and progress logs to ensure complete functionality over low-bandwidth mobile networks connections**

  - The system shall execute Vosk speech recognition entirely on-device without requiring an active network connection. 

## 3.2 Functional Requirements
**Content Structure**: The applications will be organized by language. Each language contains 3 Modules: Introduction, Navigation, and Business. Each Module consists of Lessons, Classes, and a Test. Classes use flash cards, fill in blank exercises, and pronunciation practice to build basic vocabulary and grammar towards the phrases a traveler needs to communicate in a country they have never been to. At the end, there will be a test at the end of each module that asses the Users' progress.

**System Functionality:** The requirements below are organized by system component. They describe what the system does, separate from the content hierarchy. The application is built with Flutter, uses Supabase (PostgreSQL) as its backend, and uses Vosk for speech recognition.

## 3.2.1 Component 1: Flashcard-Based Vocabulary and Grammar
### 3.2.1.1 Purpose & Overview
This component manages interactive two-sided flashcards for both vocabulary acquisition and grammar instruction. It delivers audio pronunciations, supports touch gesture navigation, implements the Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler (FSRS) algorithm for memory retention, and enables full offline learning capability backed by cloud synchronization.

### 3.2.1.2 Stimulus / Response Sequence
- **Stimulus**: User opens a Class or initiates a due review session. 	

- **Response**: System fetches flashcard data (text, translations, and Mozilla Common Voice audio references) from local storage or Supabase and renders the first card's front face. 

- **Stimulus**: User taps the card surface. 		

- **Response**: System flips the card to reveal the reverse face with the native translation, grammar notes, and audio playback controls. 

- **Stimulus**: User selects a recall rating (Again, Hard, Good, or Easy). 	

- **Response**: System calculates the next review parameters using FSRS, updates local storage and Supabase, and advances to the next card. 

### 3.2.1.3 Functional Requirements
- **Card Content & Multi-Sided Display**

  - The system shall display two-sided flashcards where the front face renders target language text/phrases and the reverse face renders the native translation, grammar explanations, and native audio playback controls.

- **Flip Gesture Interaction	**

  - The system shall toggle the 	flashcard display between front and reverse faces upon detecting a user tap gesture on the card area. 

- **Navigation Mechanics**

  - The system shall allow users to navigate sequentially between flashcards using horizontal swipe gestures or on-screen arrow controls. 

- **Order Randomization	**

  - The system shall provide a shuffle option to randomize the card presentation order within an active set. 

- **Progress Indicator**

  - The system shall display a real-time progress indicator showing the number of remaining cards in the active lesson or review session. 

- **Recall Assessment & FSRS Spaced Repetition**

  - The system shall prompt the user to rate their recall difficulty (*Again*, *Hard*, *Good*, or *Easy*) after flipping a card. 

  - The system shall execute the Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler (FSRS) algorithm to calculate each 	card's next review date, difficulty, stability, and last review timestamp based on user ratings. 		

- **Filtering & Due Review Sessions	**

  - The system shall allow users to initiate review sessions containing exclusively cards that are currently due according to FSRS metrics. 	

  - The system shall allow users to filter card sets to display only unlearned cards based on historical FSRS data. 		

- **Unified Grammar Card Design	**

  - The system shall apply identical flashcard display mechanics, navigation controls, and 	FSRS scheduling rules to grammar-focused card sets. 		

- **Asset Integration & Offline Persistence**

  - The system shall fetch flashcard text, translations, and Mozilla Common Voice audio references from the Supabase database. 

  - The system shall persist user review parameters (due date, difficulty, stability, and review history) in the local device storage for offline access and sync changes with Supabase when online. 

## 3.2.2 Component 2: Fill-in-the-Blank Sentence Exercises
### 3.2.2.1 Purpose & Overview
This component presents interactive sentence completion exercises designed to build target language grammar and sentence structure skills. It displays sentences with missing target words, provides a tap-to-select word bank with distractor options, supports audio playback of full sentences, and delivers instant visual and explanatory feedback upon submission.

### 3.2.2.2 Stimulus / Response Sequence
- **Stimulus:** User initiates a fill-in-the-blank exercise within an active lesson or 	test.

- **Response:** System loads target sentence data (sourced from Tatoeba), renders blank slots, generates a randomized word tile bank containing correct answers and distractors, and displays sentence audio controls.

- **Stimulus**: User taps a word tile from the bank.

- **Response**: System places the selected tile into the first available blank slot in the sentence.

- **Stimulus**: User taps an occupied blank slot or selected tile.

- **Response:** System removes the tile from the blank slot and returns it to the selectable word bank.

- **Stimulus:** User taps the "Check" or "Submit" button.

- **Response:** System evaluates the assembled sentence against the solution key, displays green success or red error feedback, plays sentence audio, and displays remedial explanations if incorrect. 	

### 3.2.2.3 Functional Requirements
- **Sentence & Blank Rendering**

  - The system shall display target language sentences containing one or more blank slots replacing specific target vocabulary or grammar words (sourced from the Tatoeba sentence dataset).

- **Word Tile Bank Generation**

  - The system shall display a word bank beneath the sentence prompt containing interactive tiles representing the correct target words alongside incorrect distractor tiles.

- **Tap-Based Tile Selection**

  - The system shall populate blank sentence slots sequentially with selected word tiles upon detecting user tap gestures on word bank tiles, without requiring typed text input.

- **Tile Deselection & Reordering	**

  - The system shall allow users to remove selected tiles from blank slots and return them to the word bank by tapping the slot prior to final submission. 

- **Sentence Audio Playback**

  - The system shall provide an audio control button that plays the complete, spoken target language sentence aloud upon user selection. 		

- Response Evaluation & Visual Feedback

  - The system shall evaluate submitted tile sequences against the correct sentence key upon user submission.

  - The system shall render green visual highlighting for correct answers and red visual highlighting for incorrect answers.

- **Remedial Explanations & Solution Display**

  - The system shall display the correct sentence order alongside a concise grammar/vocabulary explanation whenever an incorrect response is submitted. 		
## 3.2.3 Component 3: Pronunciation Practice
### 3.2.3.1 Purpose & Overview
This component facilitates interactive oral speech practice by prompting users to read target language phrases aloud. It captures user speech, processes audio strictly on-device using the local Vosk engine (ensuring privacy and offline capability), evaluates pronunciation accuracy against expected text prompts via a similarity threshold, delivers visual pass/fail feedback, and supports seamless engine modularity (e.g., swappability with OpenAI Whisper).
### 3.2.3.2 Stimulus / Response Sequence
- **Stimulus**: User initiates a pronunciation exercise in an active class or test.

- **Response:** System displays the target text prompt, native audio sample button, and microphone record control. 	

- **Stimulus**: User taps the native audio button. 	

- **Response**: System plays the pre-recorded reference pronunciation clip. 	

- **Stimulus**: User taps the microphone button to start and stop recording. 	

- **Response**: System captures voice audio, 	transcribes it locally using the Vosk engine, evaluates similarity 	against the target phrase, displays visual pass/fail feedback, and enables retry or next-exercise controls. 	

### 3.2.3.3 Functional Requirements
- **Target Prompt & Reference Audio**

  - The system shall display target-language words or phrases alongside an audio playback control button that plays the native pronunciation clip upon user selection. 

- On-Device Audio Recording Controls

  - The system shall provide a touch-controlled microphone button to start and stop the voice recording of the user's pronunciation attempt.

- Local Speech Transcription (Privacy & Offline)

  - The system shall transcribe recorded speech locally on the mobile device using the embedded Vosk speech recognition engine, ensuring voice audio is never transmitted or uploaded over a network for evaluation.

- **Similarity Threshold Evaluation & Scoring	**

  - The system shall compare the generated text transcription against the expected target phrase using a defined text similarity threshold to determine a Pass 	or Fail result. 	

- **Visual Feedback & Unlimited Practice Retries**

  - The system shall display clear visual feedback indicators corresponding to the evaluated Pass or Fail status.

  - The system shall allow users unlimited recording retries prior to advancing to the next exercise. 

- **Speech Recognition Engine Modularity**

  - The system shall decouple the speech evaluation interface from the underlying ASR model architecture, allowing technical replacement of the Vosk engine (e.g., with OpenAI Whisper) without altering exercise behavior or UI flows.

- Permission & Model Failure Fallbacks

  - The system shall display an informative fallback error message if device microphone permissions are denied or if the local speech model fails to initialize.	

  - The system shall provide options to re-request permissions, retry model loading, or skip the pronunciation exercise without halting lesson progression. 
## 3.2.4 Component 4: Module Tests
### 3.2.4.1 Purpose & Overview
This component provides summative evaluation of user language mastery at the conclusion of each Module (Introduction, Navigation, and Business). It enforces prerequisite curriculum completion, delivers multiple-choice assessment items across image-based, real-world scenario, and listening comprehension modalities, provides immediate per-item feedback alongside cumulative scoring, and synchronizes results with progress analytics.
### 3.2.4.2 Stimulus / Response Sequence
- **Stimulus:** User attempts to access a Module Test. 

- **Response**: System checks completion status of all preceding Lessons and Classes within the target Module, unlocking the test if prerequisites are met or displaying a lock indicator if incomplete. 

- **Stimulus:** User initiates an unlocked Module Test. 

- **Response:** System fetches test question items (Wikimedia images, scenario prompts, audio clips) from local cache or Supabase and presents the first multiple choice question. 

- **Stimulus**: User selects an answer option. 	

- **Response:** System validates the response, provides immediate visual feedback (correct/incorrect indicator), and advances to the next question. 	

- **Stimulus:** User submits the final test question. 

- **Response:** System calculates the final percentage score, displays the test summary screen, saves test records to Supabase, and updates user progress analytics. 
### 3.2.4.3 Functional Requirements
- **Prerequisite Completion Gating** 

  - The system shall restrict access to a Module Test until the user has successfully completed all required Lessons and Classes within that specific Module. 		

- **Standardized Multiple-Choice Format**

  - The system shall format all 	Module Test assessment items exclusively as multiple-choice questions with single-select answer options. 

- **Image-Based Assessment Items**

  - The system shall display image-based questions featuring a visual prompt (sourced from Wikimedia) requiring the user to select the corresponding target-language word or phrase. 

- **Real-World Scenario Assessment Items**

  - The system shall present situational scenario prompts depicting real-world interactions (such as ordering food or asking for directions) requiring the user to select the contextually appropriate target-language response. 

- **Audio Listening Comprehension Items**

  - The system shall provide audio controls that play a spoken phrase or dialogue interaction requiring the user to select the correct translation, response, or meaning. 			

- **Immediate Item Feedback & Cumulative Scoring**  

  - The system shall render immediate visual feedback (correct or incorrect indicator) upon the selection of an answer choice for each test question.

  - The system shall calculate and display a final percentage score upon completion of all test items. 

- **Persistence & Analytics Integration**

  - The system shall record test attempt details (score, date, timestamp, item responses) to the Supabase database and transmit performance data to Component 6 (User Progression and Analytics).

## 3.2.5 Component 5: Onboarding and Authentication
### 3.2.5.1 Purpose & Overview
This component manages secure user registration, multi-factor/SSO authentication via Supabase Auth, persistent session management, platform keychain/keystore token security, post-signup language preference configuration, initial skill assessment onboarding, and account self-service management.

3.2.5.2 Stimulus / Response Sequence	

- **Stimulus:** User launches the app for the first time or logs out. 	

- **Response:** System displays the authentication welcome screen with options to sign up, log in, or initiate password recovery. 		

- **Stimulus:** User submits credentials or authenticates via third-party provider (Supabase Auth). 

- **Response:** System validates credentials, issues auth tokens, stores them in secure platform storage (iOS Keychain / Android Keystore), and transitions to initial setup

- **Stimulus**: New user completes registration. 

- **Response:** System prompts for target language selection, presents the optional starting experience survey, and renders the crash-course structure introduction before navigating to the main dashboard. 	

### 3.2.5.3 Functional Requirements	
- **User Registration & Third-Party Authentication**

  - The system shall allow new users to register an account by providing an email and password or by authenticating through supported third-party single sign-on (SSO) providers via Supabase Auth. 	

- **User Login & Persistent Session Management**

  - The system shall authenticate returning users against Supabase Auth credentials. 

  - The system shall maintain an active logged-in user session across application restarts until the user explicitly selects the manual logout option.

- **Secure Credential & Token Storage**

  - The system shall store authentication tokens and refresh credentials exclusively within secure OS platform storage (iOS Keychain or Android Keystore). 		

- **Password Recovery & Reset Workflow**

  - The system shall dispatch a secure password recovery email upon user request and permit the user to establish a new password upon returning to the app via the recovery link. 	

- **Post-Signup Target Language Selection & Experience Survey**

  - The system shall require newly registered users to select their active target language prior to accessing the core curriculum. 	

  - The system shall present an optional onboarding prompt inquiring about the user's prior language experience (Complete Beginner vs. Some Prior Exposure). 

- **Curriculum Structure Introduction**

  - The system shall display a brief onboarding overview explaining the crash-course modular structure (Introduction, Navigation, and Business Modules ending in summative Module Tests). 

- **Account Profile Management**

  - The system shall provide an account settings screen enabling authenticated users to update profile information and modify their account password. 		

- **User Logout**

  - The system shall provide a manual logout option within the settings screen that revokes active local session state and clears stored platform credentials. 

-  **Account Deletion Confirmation & Permanent Data Erasure**

  - The system shall provide a "Delete Account" option within the account settings screen. 

  - The system shall prompt the user for explicit confirmation with an unambiguous warning stating that deletion is permanent and cannot be undone prior to executing account deletion. 	

  - The system shall permanently erase the user's login credentials, profile details, progress data, and FSRS review schedules from the database upon deletion confirmation. 

  - The system shall automatically sign the user out and purge all local cached user data and stored platform credentials from the device following account deletion.

## 3.2.6 Component 6: User Progression and Analytics
### 3.2.6.1 Purpose & Overview
This component defines explicit completion logic across all curriculum hierarchy levels (Classes, Lessons, Modules), maintains user progress and performance weakness analytics, enforces strict row-level user data isolation within PostgreSQL, and provides offline progress caching with automatic cloud synchronization.

### 3.2.6.2 Stimulus / Response Sequence
- **Stimulus:** User finishes an exercise item, flashcard set, or Module Test. 	

- **Response:** System evaluates completion rules against current activity, updates completion metrics across Class/Lesson/Module levels, stores updated 	state in local storage, and updates dashboard visualizations. 	

- **Stimulus:** User navigates to the Progress Dashboard. 	

- **Response**: System aggregates completion percentages, historical test scores, and weakness analytics, rendering an interactive summary. 	

- **Stimulus:** Device reconnects to the network following offline usage. 	

- **Response:** System detects active connectivity and pushes queued local progress records to the user’s isolated Supabase PostgreSQL database.

### 3.2.6.3 Functional Requirements
- **Hierarchical Completion Rules**

  - The system shall mark a Flashcard Class complete once the user has provided an FSRS rating  (Again, Hard, Good, Easy) for every card in the set at least once. 		

  - The system shall mark a Fill-in-the-Blank Class complete once the user has submitted an answer for every sentence exercise in the set. 		

  - The system shall mark a Pronunciation Class to complete once the user has passed or skipped every phrase in the set. 

  - The system shall mark a Lesson complete once all contained Classes are marked complete. 	

  - The system shall mark a Module complete once the user successfully completes its corresponding Module Test.

- **Post-Completion Review Retention**

  - The system shall retain completed flashcard sets in an accessible state for ongoing FSRS review sessions regardless of overall course completion status.

- **Multi-Language Curriculum Tracking** 

  - The system shall track completed Modules (Introduction, Navigation, and Business) independently for each supported target language. 

- **Progress Dashboard Visualizations** 

  - The system shall render a central progress dashboard displaying overall completion percentages broken down per language and per Module (Introduction, Navigation, Business). 	

- **Module Test History & Score Review**

  - **The system shall record score history for every Module Test attempt and allow users to review their past test results.** 	

- **Performance Analytics & Weakness Identification** 

  - The system shall log correct and incorrect performance history across all exercise types to analyze user accuracy and identify specific weak skill areas (such as specific vocabulary items, grammar structures, or question formats). 

- **Data Isolation & Row-Level Security**

  -  ****The system shall store user progress records in a Supabase PostgreSQL database configured with strict security policies ensuring users can access and modify exclusively their own data records. 

- **Offline Progress Caching & Synchronization**

  - The system shall persist in activity logs and completion of metrics in local device storage when operating offline. 

  - The system shall automatically upload and synchronize cached progress data with the Supabase database upon restoration of network connectivity.

## 
## 3.3 Performance Requirements
- **Application Cold Startup Latency**

  - The system shall launch and render the primary dashboard (or login screen for unauthenticated sessions) within 3.0 seconds of application initiation on supported iOS and Android smartphone hardware. 	

- **User Interface Touch Response Time**

  - The system shall process and render local UI state transitions—including touch-based flashcard flips and tap-to-select word-tile movements—within 100 milliseconds of detecting a user tap gesture. 

- **Pronunciation Speech Processing Latency**

  - The system shall transcribe 	captured speech, evaluate pronunciation accuracy, and display visual pass/fail feedback within 2.0 seconds after the user stops recording.

- **Audio Playback Initiation & Local Buffering**

  - The system shall initiate native audio playback within 500 milliseconds of a user pressing an audio control button. 

  - The system shall pre-buffer all required audio clips into local memory upon opening a Lesson, ensuring audio playback operates independently of network latencies. 

- **Initial Lesson Content Download Speed** 

  - The system shall fetch, parse, and render complete Lesson text, exercise metadata, and asset references from the cloud backend within 3.0 seconds over a standard Wi-Fi connection. 

- **Network-Independent Offline Exercise Execution**

  - The system shall execute all interactive exercises (flashcards, fill-in-the-blanks, and pronunciation practice) locally on the device once Lesson content is loaded, without issuing additional network requests during exercise completion. 
## 3.4 Logical Database Requirements
### 3.4.1 Database Architecture & Technology
    - **Managed Database Engine & Storage Architectur**

    - The system shall utilize Supabase managed PostgreSQL as its primary relational database management system (RDBMS).

    - The system shall store binary media files (audio clips and images) in Supabase Cloud Storage, while storing uniform resource identifiers (URIs) and file metadata references within PostgreSQL database tables.
### 3.4.2 Logical Data Entities & Schemas
- **User Accounts & Profiles Schema**

  - The database shall store user profile records, including: Selected target language Starting experience level (Complete Beginner vs. Some Prior Exposure). User settings for Sign-in credential authentication shall be handled via Supabase Auth.

- **Curriculum & Content Schema**

  - The database shall store hierarchical curriculum content comprising: Languages, Modules (Introduction, Navigation, and Business),  Lessons, Classes, Flashcards, Fill-in-the-blank sentences (sourced from Tatoeba), and  Module Test question sets

- **Media Asset & Attribution Metadata Schema**

  - The database shall store metadata records for all sentences, audio clips, and images, including explicit source provenance, copyright/license details, and required attribution display text (e.g., Wikimedia, Mozilla Common Voice).

- **User Progress, Performance & FSRS Schedule Schema**

  - The database shall store historical user progress data, 		including completed Classes, Lessons, and Tests, historical test 		scores, item-level response logs, and per-card FSRS review 		parameters (due date, difficulty, stability, and last review 		timestamp).
### 3.4.3 Relationships, Data Security & Access Control
- **Entity Hierarchy & Referential Integrity**

  - The database shall enforce hierarchical relationships where each Module belongs to exactly one 	Language, and each Lesson, Class, and exercise item belongs to exactly one Module. 

  - The database shall enforce strict foreign-key integrity where each user progress record belongs to exactly one authenticated user account. 

- **Row-Level Security (RLS) & Access Permissions**

  - The system shall enforce Row-Level Security (RLS) policies within PostgreSQL ensuring authenticated users can read and write exclusively their own user progress, score history, and FSRS review schedules.

  - The system shall enforce strict read-only access permissions on all curriculum content, lesson structures, and asset metadata for standard user accounts.
### 3.4.4 Offline Persistence & Synchronization
- **Local Database Caching & Sync Protocol**

  - The system shall maintain a local database cache on the mobile client storing pending user progress logs and updated FSRS schedules during offline operation. 		

  - The system shall automatically synchronize locally cached 		records with the remote PostgreSQL database upon network 		restoration.
## 3.5 Design Constraints and Standards Compliance
### 3.5.1 Technology & Architecture Constraints
- **Single Codebase Cross-Platform Architecture**

  - The system shall be developed using the Flutter framework to generate natively compiled applications for both iOS and Android platforms from a unified codebase. 

- Backend Infrastructure Binding

  - The system shall utilize Supabase services exclusively for authentication, cloud database operations (PostgreSQL), and media asset file storage.

- Modular On-Device Speech Engine

  - The system shall integrate the Vosk speech recognition engine for local processing while maintaining a decoupled software interface that allows replacement of the speech model without altering user-facing exercise behavior.
### 3.5.2 Regulatory & Mobile Store Policy Compliance
- **App Store Guidelines & Privacy Disclosures**

  - The system shall comply with all Apple App Store Review Guidelines and Google Play Developer Program Policies, including mandatory privacy policy disclosures, data safety declarations, and user data handling rules. 

- **Platform-Native Navigation Standards**

  - The system shall adhere to platform-specific interaction 		standards, supporting the Android system back button/gesture and 		the iOS edge swipe-back gesture seamlessly. 
### 3.5.3 Privacy, Permissions & Security Constraints
- **Dynamic Microphone Permission Request**

  - The system shall request device microphone permission upon the user's initial entry into a pronunciation exercise, presenting a brief explanation of why audio access is required, and executing the fallback behavior specified in section 3.2.3.3 for permission denied.

- **Audio Ephemerality & Local Privacy**

  - The system shall process recorded user speech entirely 	on-device and shall purge all recorded voice audio from volatile memory immediately after pronunciation evaluation, ensuring zero audio storage. 
### 3.5.4 Open Data & Intellectual Property Licensing
- **Third-Party Asset Licensing & Attribution**

  - The system shall consume sentence datasets, audio clips, and images within the exact copyright license terms of their 	respective source repositories (Tatoeba, Mozilla Common Voice, and Wikimedia Commons) and render explicit attribution text where required by license agreements. 
### 3.5.5 Accessibility & Universal Design Standards
- **Screen Reader & Dynamic Text Accessibility**

  - The system shall be fully compatible with platform screen readers (Apple VoiceOver on iOS and Google TalkBack on Android) and automatically adjust UI layouts to 	accommodate user-selected system font scaling settings. 

- **Color-Independent Feedback Visuals**

  - The system shall deliver exercise correctness feedback using multimodal indicators (combining icons or text labels alongside color changes) so that visual status never relies on color perception alone. 

- **Contrast Ratios & Touch Target Metrics**

  - The system shall maintain a minimum body text contrast ratio of **4.5:1** against visual backgrounds. 		

  - The system shall enforce minimum interactive touch target dimensions of **44 × 44 points** on iOS devices and **48 × 48 density-independent pixels (dp)** on Android devices.

## 4. Software System Attributes (Non-Functional Requirements)
###    
### 4.1 Reliability & Availability: 
- The system shall run pronunciation recognition on-device (Vosk), so speech practice does not depend on cloud availability.

- The system shall resume interrupted background asset downloads without restarting them.

- The system shall target 99.9% monthly availability for its cloud services (Supabase Auth, database, and storage).

- The system shall rely on Supabase's managed, redundant infrastructure for authentication and data services instead of self-hosted login servers.

- The system shall keep every lesson, flashcard, fill-in-the-blank, and pronunciation exercise usable without a network connection once the lesson content has been loaded.

- The system shall cache progress and FSRS review data locally and sync it automatically when connectivity returns, with no loss of progress.
###  4.2 Robustness & Error Handling: 
- The system shall display a non-blocking on-screen alert when internet connectivity is lost: "No internet connection. Your progress is saved on this device and will sync when you reconnect."

-  The system shall keep the user in the current exercise when connectivity drops and shall not discard answers or progress. 

- The system shall display a clear message when microphone permission is denied or the speech model fails, and shall offer the options to re-request permission, retry, or skip the exercise.

- The system shall show a user-friendly message with a retry option when a Supabase request, login attempt, or lesson download fails, and shall never expose raw error codes or stack traces to the user. 

- The system shall validate all user input (email format, password strength, required fields) before submitting it to the backend. 

- The system shall recover from an unexpected app closure by restoring the user's last saved progress when the app is reopened.
###    4.3 Security & Privacy: 
- The system shall authenticate users with email and password or SSO through Supabase Auth and shall support multi-factor authentication (a one-time verification code) as an additional login step. 

- The system shall store session tokens only in the iOS Keychain or Android Keystore.

- The system shall encrypt all communication between the app and its services using HTTPS with TLS 1.3. 

- The system shall route Azure Speech requests through a Supabase Edge Function so that API keys are never stored in the client app.

- The system shall enforce row-level security so that each user can access only their own profile and progress data.

- The system shall process recorded voice only in device memory and shall delete it immediately after evaluation; no audio recordings are stored or transmitted.

- The system shall request microphone permission only when the user first enters a pronunciation exercise, with a short explanation of why it is needed. 

- The system shall let users delete their account, which permanently erases their server-side data and purges all locally stored data. 

- The system shall support VoiceOver and TalkBack so that users can operate the app through voice and speech accessibility features.
###    4.4 Maintainability: 
- The system shall be built as a single Flutter codebase organized into the six Components (Flashcards, Fill-in-the-Blank, Pronunciation, Module Tests, Onboarding/Authentication, and Progression/Analytics), so each can be modified or tested independently.

-   The system shall keep the speech recognition engine behind a swappable interface so that Vosk can be replaced with Whisper without changing the Pronunciation Component's exercise logic.

- The system shall manage database schema changes through versioned Supabase migrations. 

- The system shall store curriculum content (Languages, Modules, Lessons, Classes, and Tests) in the database, so content can be added or corrected without releasing a new app version. 

-  The system shall keep source attribution and license metadata for Tatoeba, Mozilla Common Voice, and Wikimedia content so that attribution can be maintained as content changes. 

- The system shall document third-party dependencies (Flutter packages, Vosk, and FSRS) and their versions so that updates can be reviewed and applied in a controlled way.
###   4.5 Usability: 
- The system shall let a first-time user complete sign-up, language selection, and onboarding within 3 minutes.

-  The system shall let a user complete a single Class within 5 to 10 minutes, so lessons fit into short study sessions before a trip. 

- The system shall use consistent navigation and layout across all Components, so a user who has learned one exercise type can use the others without further instruction.

-  The system shall give immediate feedback on every exercise (correct/incorrect, pass/fail) in a form that does not depend on color alone. 

- The system shall support font scaling, a 4.5:1 minimum text contrast ratio, and minimum touch targets of 44x44 pt (iOS) and 48x48 dp (Android). 

- The system shall support platform-standard navigation, including the Android back button and the iOS swipe-back gesture.
###    4.6 Portability: 
- The system shall run on both Android and iOS from a single Flutter codebase, with platform-specific code limited to the Keychain/Keystore, microphone permissions, and similar native integrations. -

-  The system shall access all backend services through Supabase's REST APIs and PostgreSQL, so that no server-side change is required to support an additional platform. 

- The system shall keep content and progress data independent of the device, so a user who signs in on a new device can continue where they left off.
